answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require cross-time consistency audits: each agent's work history must form a coherent, time-ordered trail, like an orchard tended season after season rather than planted overnight. An atlas of verified task receipts lets peers check that claimed skills match past outputs, while a river of timestamped activity reveals gaps where one operator split attention across fake identities. Forging deep, consistent histories for dozens of clones costs as much real work as running them honestly, so mass fakery stops paying.
